# Decisions: duel-online

From the operator's grill session of 2026-09-24, after slices 1 and 2 (duel core, sea) merged into `main`.

## Decisions

- Duel entry: a standalone Colyseus duel room joined by its own code, plus a practice mode against a server-side dummy. It hosts the same duel simulation object that `MatchRoom` will embed in `encounters-theft` (§14). This keeps the spike isolated from the sea and from reservations, transitions and theft.
- Netcode: §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback. Clients predict with the shared `stepDuel`; the server sends checkpoints and input acknowledgements, and a mismatch restores the checkpoint and replays. The shared input delay is 3–8 frames, chosen per duel from measured latency. This is the part the spike exists to prove; a plain input-delay model was rejected because its findings would not carry over.
- Wire protocol, revised after design challenge attempt 1 (P1: one input message per frame would hit the unchanged 60-per-second gate cap and drop real presses). Clients send batched, redundant inputs (the last few frames per message, at most 30 messages a second). The server sends one frame bundle per cadence with the inputs it applied, substitutions included, plus a snapshot every second bundle or a hash otherwise. The client rolls back as soon as a confirmed input differs from its prediction; the snapshot is the authority and the desync detector. This is one message type in each direction and one code path to prove.
- The rollback core is a single pure module, `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/netcode`, used by both the browser and the headless harness client (challenge P1: otherwise the harness would prove a reimplementation, not the client the operator plays). It follows the purity rules, with the caller supplying time.
- Evidence must not be trivial: clients compare the hash of their own simulated state at snapshot frames, before restoring anything, and the harness proxy never reorders and turns loss into a head-of-line stall.
- One fullstack lane (`duel`). A lane can't compile against another lane's new types, and the arena, the netcode and the room share new protocol types.
- The spike's exit (§18) is judged by the operator's playtest after the run: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect must feel credible at §19's latencies. The run delivers the automated evidence (hash agreement and bounded corrections through the impairment harness) and the dev latency setting the playtest needs.
- The sea's density problem (224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, 10-tile sight radius) is deferred to `encounters-theft`, where sight, speed and travel times can be tuned against real encounters.
- Tests drive input like players do (held keys, short taps, the throw chord with rollover), after world-sea's docking bug passed every check with idealised input.

## Assumptions

- Checkpoints and inputs travel as Colyseus messages over the existing reliable WebSocket; the room's synced Schema state is not used for the duel's frame data. Head-of-line stalls from loss are exactly what the harness measures.
- The duel room reuses the input gate's limits (size, rate, sequence, future frames) with a duel input schema.
- `packages/test-tools` may now depend on `@pirate-sea-race/simulation` (for the replay wrapper and the headless duel client), because this feature owns the lockfile.
- Rates the worker chooses and documents: checkpoint frequency (for example every 6 frames), the input forwarding cadence, and the correction threshold used in the harness test.
- The dummy's behaviour (idle or guarding) is a practice-mode option, not an AI.

## Deferred

- Embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, grapples and challenges, reservations and the 3-second transition from the sea, theft and respawn: `encounters-theft`.
- Haki abilities, fruit kits, art, animation and sound.
- Duel spectating (§6 defers it).
- Tuning the input-delay policy after the playtest (§15 "Tune this policy in the spike"): a follow-up if the playtest asks for it.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

331	## 12 Defeat disconnection and failure
332	
333	| Event | Required behavior |
334	| --- | --- |
335	| Normal duel loss | Transfer one eligible rubbing and gold; retain kit; respawn after 15 seconds |
336	| Disconnect in world | Cancel channels; avatar remains vulnerable; reserve seat for 60 seconds |
337	| Disconnect in duel | Neutral inputs after held-input timeout; fight continues; forfeit after 10 seconds absent |
338	| Return within reservation | Reattach same player identity to the current authoritative state |
339	| Reservation expires | Drop remaining rubbings into a visible recovery cache; remove player |
340	| Explicit quit | Immediate duel forfeit if needed; then release remaining rubbings into a cache |
341	| Server process failure | Abort affected match in first release; no winner or competitive penalty |
342	| Both duel clients absent | Cancel unresolved rewards if both forfeit on the same tick; release caches on expiry |
343	
344	### Details that prevent exploits
345	
346	After 250 milliseconds without a valid input stream, clear held movement and attack buttons. Disconnecting cannot keep a character attacking indefinitely, pause the match, or protect their inventory. A disconnected world avatar can be challenged; if they remain absent, the ordinary forfeit rule applies.
347	
348	If a disconnected player loses a duel, process the normal one-rubbing transfer first, move the player to their respawn state, and preserve the original seat-reservation deadline. At expiry, place their remaining rubbings in a recovery cache at that respawn dock. Do not duplicate the already-transferred rubbing.
349	
350	A cache is placed on the nearest reachable shoreline or dock if its intended position is invalid. It never despawns during the match. Each rubbing can be collected only by a player missing that type. A six-second interaction claims one selected rubbing at a time. An empty cache disappears.
351	
352	### Server health versus individual connection quality
353	
354	Individual packet loss is not a reason to cancel a losing fight. A server-detected simulation stall affecting the encounter is a separate fault. Cancel that duel without transfers, restore both pre-duel inventories, and return participants safely. Log the fault and match revision.
355	
356	The first release stores final outcomes, not resumable live-world snapshots. A process restart cannot be described as a reconnect recovery. Add crash recovery only after the basic match and transaction model are proven. If everyone leaves, close the room and mark it abandoned with no winner.
357	
358	## 13 Interface art and sound
359	
360	| Screen | Information or action it must support |
361	| --- | --- |
362	| Landing and lobby | Play, private code, region, ping, settings, and short rules |
363	| Overworld HUD | Four symbol slots, compass, minimap, gold, protection timer, match clock |
364	| Journal | Known islands, collected types, current rumors, and power descriptions |
365	| Duel HUD | Two health bars, stamina, Haki, round clock, and connection indicator |
366	| Duel result | Winner, exact item transfer, and respawn or return countdown |
367	| Final race | Treasure eligibility, visible claim progress, and interruption feedback |
368	| Match result | Winner or timeout, route history, duels, stolen and recovered clues |
369	
370	### Onboarding and accessibility
371	
372	Offer a five-minute solo introduction: move, sail, dock, complete a ruin, guard a heavy, punish it, and understand theft. Let experienced players skip it. Provide a practice arena with an idle or scripted defensive opponent, hitbox visualization for developers, and a reset button.
373	
374	Use shapes and names as well as colors for rubbing types. Allow larger UI, reduced screen shake, reduced flashing, separate audio sliders, and full control remapping. Supply visual equivalents for grapple warnings and claim alarms. Ensure menus work with keyboard navigation and use readable DOM text where practical.
375	
376	### Visual direction and production budget
377	
378	Use a coherent original 2D anime-pirate style with strong silhouettes, bright seas, and readable island themes. Start with one shared humanoid rig or sprite base and cosmetic variations. Ship-deck and island duels share one collision layout with two backgrounds. Save unusual body proportions and bespoke movesets for later.
379	
380	Budget roughly 18–24 shared character animation actions, plus fruit-specific effects and any required unique poses. Track walk, crouch, jump, dash, guard, hit reactions, knockdown, throw, normals, and specials in an asset manifest. A generated concept image is not a finished gameplay sprite set; animation consistency and hitbox alignment need production work.
381	
382	Sound should communicate interaction timing: distinct cues for launch, impact, guard, parry, grapple warning, rubbing theft, and a full set. Unlock browser audio after the player’s first input. The initial client should preload shared combat assets and stream optional island decoration later. Art cannot delay the first control response by requiring the whole world to load.
383	
384	## 14 Browser architecture

| Event | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Normal duel loss | Transfer one eligible rubbing and gold; retain kit; respawn after 15 seconds |
| Disconnect in world | Cancel channels; avatar remains vulnerable; reserve seat for 60 seconds |
| Disconnect in duel | Neutral inputs after held-input timeout; fight continues; forfeit after 10 seconds absent |
| Return within reservation | Reattach same player identity to the current authoritative state |

| Explicit quit | Immediate duel forfeit if needed; then release remaining rubbings into a cache |

### Details that prevent exploits

After 250 milliseconds without a valid input stream, clear held movement and attack buttons. Disconnecting cannot keep a character attacking indefinitely, pause the match, or protect their inventory. A disconnected world avatar can be challenged; if they remain absent, the ordinary forfeit rule applies.

If a disconnected player loses a duel, process the normal one-rubbing transfer first, move the player to their respawn state, and preserve the original seat-reservation deadline. At expiry, place their remaining rubbings in a recovery cache at that respawn dock. Do not duplicate the already-transferred rubbing.

A cache is placed on the nearest reachable shoreline or dock if its intended position is invalid. It never despawns during the match. Each rubbing can be collected only by a player missing that type. A six-second interaction claims one selected rubbing at a time. An empty cache disappears.

Individual packet loss is not a reason to cancel a losing fight. A server-detected simulation stall affecting the encounter is a separate fault. Cancel that duel without transfers, restore both pre-duel inventories, and return participants safely. Log the fault and match revision.
